findings.title: Legacy HTTP snapshots are falsely accepted
findings.why_it_matters: The exact-round-trip gate declares a registration with `transport.type === "http"` restorable, but restore uses `codex mcp add --url`, whose current CLI creates a streamable HTTP registration. On a later failure, the installer has already removed the original, recreates it with a different transport type, then fails its equality check and leaves the user with altered client state and an incomplete rollback.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject `http` snapshots unless Codex exposes an add mode that preserves that exact type, and add a legacy-HTTP fixture that proves forced replacement is refused before any mutation.
evidence: codex_snapshot_is_cli_restorable accepts both `streamable_http` and `http` at line 605.
restore_codex_json converts either accepted type to the same `codex mcp add --url` invocation at lines 647-649.
The current `codex mcp add --help` identifies `--url` as a streamable HTTP server, while restore_codex_json's equality check at lines 657-658 requires the original type to round-trip unchanged.

findings.title: Missing other CLI bypasses path coherence
findings.why_it_matters: A targeted diagrams-path change still succeeds when the unselected client binary and skill are absent even if its old installer-created registration remains persisted. When that client becomes available again it keeps pointing to the old diagram directory, contradicting the coherence guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Inspect the unselected client's persisted registration without requiring its executable where possible, or conservatively refuse the path change when the other client cannot be checked; cover the missing-CLI/absent-skill/retained-registration case.
evidence: For a Codex-targeted change, the only registration check is inside `command -v claude` at lines 444-449; when Claude is absent and its skill is absent, `other_owned` remains zero and line 468 permits the change.
The Claude registration is stored in CLAUDE_USER_CONFIG_FILE and survives removal or temporary absence of the CLI binary.
The Claude-targeted/Codex-unavailable case repeats the same bypass at lines 458-463.

residual_risks: The deleted-registration resurrection fix now distinguishes a confirmed missing registration from an unreadable state and preserves a deletion made after a successful add; the supplied deterministic Codex test covers that path.

Post-add verification records a successful add before reading it and rechecks the desired registration before commit, so a transient read failure or late replacement enters rollback rather than silently committing it.
Registration compare/remove operations are still inherently TOCTOU with independent client-config writers after the final read and before the remove command.
testing_gaps: No fixture covers a legacy Codex `transport.type: http` snapshot, despite it being accepted by the restorable-snapshot predicate.
No targeted path-change test combines a missing unselected CLI, an absent unselected skill, and a retained unselected registration.
